projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The persistent ~20–25 connected mobile devices on a typical school/work Monday afternoon, paired with zero camera motion and a gradual declining trend, strongly indicates stationary IoT devices or a network artifact rather than actual occupancy. This pattern suggests a transient connectivity state rather than a gathering, but verifying the network is recommended to rule out ghost devices or security risks.

The consistent ~20 connected devices on a Monday afternoon with zero camera activity strongly suggests a work-from-home day or house guests, with occupants staying in private rooms rather than common areas. This explains the quiet home signals and confirms the house is occupied despite the lack of visible movement.

The persistent ~20 device count on a Monday morning, combined with zero camera or activity signals, strongly suggests IoT devices are being miscounted as mobile presence rather than actual household occupancy, indicating the presence data may be unreliable for occupancy tracking.

The consistent presence of ~20 mobile devices on a Monday morning contradicts the expected school/work schedule and lacks corresponding camera activity, strongly suggesting a network scanning artifact or presence detection misconfiguration rather than actual occupants. This should be verified to prevent false alerts and ensure accurate home automation triggers.

The stable presence count (25–26 devices), zero camera motion, and concurrent sleep data syncs confirm the household is in a normal nighttime rest cycle, with no signs of late-night activity, guests, or connectivity issues.

The sustained 19–23 connected devices paired with zero indoor camera motion over four hours suggests the household is likely stationary in a single, unmonitored area (such as the living room or backyard) or that motion detection is inactive. A quick camera check is recommended to ensure proper coverage and prevent automation blind spots.

The stable 19–21 device count paired with zero indoor camera motion over the last four hours confirms the household is settled indoors with minimal movement, consistent with a relaxed Sunday evening routine. This cross-signal pattern indicates normal occupancy rather than a sensor or presence anomaly.

The sustained 19–24 device count paired with zero indoor camera motion strongly suggests the household is gathered outdoors rather than inside, or indicates a network/presence tracking anomaly. Given the unusually high device count for a family of four, a quick verification is recommended to rule out a false signal or unlogged guests.

The sustained 22–24 device count paired with zero camera motion strongly suggests a large, stationary gathering rather than typical movement, but the unusually high count warrants verifying that all connections are legitimate guests to rule out unauthorized network access.

The sustained 22–27 device count over four hours on a Sunday afternoon, paired with zero camera triggers, strongly indicates a large gathering is occurring in camera-blind zones rather than a network glitch. This matters because it confirms an active event in unmonitored areas, prompting Steve to verify guest locations and ensure perimeter/security cameras are operational.
